items.title: Jane Ira Bloom interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 3, 1998
items.q: I started working with an improvisational dance company, which was run by a choreographer named Richard Bull. And I spent many years performing with them

ctx.x: I forgot to ask you about your Pilobolus. That must have been fun, huh?

Well I met the Pilobolus Company in 1979 when I lived in New Haven and they worked out of Connecticut. So one of the dancers, Allison Chase, became aware of my work and she wanted a solo saxophone score for her new solo piece that she had done, it was later called “Moonblind.” So we spent a lot of weeks working in her studio. I loved it. And I didn’t realize at the time how much I loved modern dance and working with dancers. And as time moved on, when I got to New York, I started working with an improvisational…
It must be a thrill to write something that has some longevity to it like that, that goes out and is spread around.
